svg.title: Unlocking the Blueprint of Life: From DNA (1953) to Genomic Medicine
svg.desc: Four-stage scientific progression diagram for Edexcel GCSE Medicine: 1. 1952 X-Ray Crystallography (Rosalind Franklin and Maurice Wilkins, Photo 51 at King's College London), 2. 1953 Double Helix Model (James Watson and Francis Crick at Cambridge, A-T and C-G base pairs), 3. 1990-2003 Human Genome Project (~3 billion base pairs and ~20,000 genes), and 4. Modern Clinical Impact and Limits (BRCA1/BRCA2 screening, cystic fibrosis, Down's syndrome, pharmacogenomics, and gene therapy), plus an Edexcel exam distinction banner clarifying DNA applies to hereditary/genetic disorders, not infectious bacterial diseases.
svg.text: EDEXCEL GCSE HISTORY · MODERN MEDICINE & GENETIC AETIOLOGY (c.1900–PRESENT)

Down's still have no genetic cure.
Exam Distinction: Discovering DNA transformed diagnosis and screening of hereditary/genetic disorders, NOT infectious bacterial diseases.
✓ WHAT DNA & GENOMICS EXPLAINED (INTERNAL HEREDITARY CODE)
Inherited / Genetic Disorders: Cystic fibrosis, Huntington's disease, sickle-cell
anaemia, Down's syndrome & inherited BRCA1/2 cancer susceptibility.
✗ COMMON EXAM TRAP — NOT CAUSED OR CURED BY DNA
Infectious Pathogens: Cholera, tuberculosis, sepsis & MRSA are caused by
external microbes (Germ Theory) and treated with antibiotics / vaccines, not DNA.
